graph.title: Zorch
notes: Page 2 is the cover/warning plus steps 1-3; pages 3-4 hold steps 4-7.
Step 2 layering is inferred: two light-gray socket plates sit on the red 2x2 plate, and two dark-gray towball plates sit on top of them.
The 1x2 side-stud brick (11211) is placed in step 3 and I joined it to both dark-gray plates. Its exact position is uncertain.

The wedge plates, clip plates and curved bricks in steps 4 and 5 are identified from small diagrams, so their types and attach points are best guesses. The wedge plates take the parts-list colour (Dark Red) even though they look red.
The black bracket 44728 appears already built in step 6, with no step of its own. I assumed it fits on the side studs of the 11211 brick.
Step 7: the inverted red bracket 99207 is joined to the black bracket.
Several edges have null ports because the exact stud positions are ambiguous.
Step 8 adds a dark red wedge plate 2x4. I assumed it sits on the studs of the inverted red bracket (b15), which is a guess.
Step 9 shows no new piece. It looks like a rotated view of the same model.
Step 10 is also a rotated view. Step 11 adds one dark red cheese slope on the wedge plate.
Step 12 looks like another view and may show a second slope. I only recorded the one slope that step 11 clearly adds.

Step 13 builds a sub-assembly of a small red clip piece with the black handlebars. I identified the red piece as the 1x1 tile with clip (12825) and placed it on the wedge plate. The handlebars are held in its clip.
Stud positions are approximate.
Step 14 adds two eyes (white Technic ball joints with eye print). Their sockets aren't visible, so I joined them to the two light-gray socket plates (b2, b3) in the body. This is a guess.

Step 15 shows the white tri-tooth plate already in place, and the callout shows a red 30° 1x2 slope. I recorded the tooth plate as sitting on the black bracket and the slope as sitting on the tooth plate. These placements are uncertain.
Step 16 has no callout. It seems to show a dark red curved band and a dark red wedge at the front, but I couldn't identify the pieces, so I added nothing for it.

Page 10 starts a leg sub-assembly, shown only as a callout with no attachment yet. It has a dark gray towball plate, a red 65° slope on top, a dark red cheese slope on the slope and an inverted red slope underneath.

The towball plate is typed 14417, but both 14417 plates are already used in the body. The body plates may actually be 14419, or the leg plate may be a different type. The leg is built once because no 2x is shown, though the parts list suggests two legs.
Page 11 step 4 adds a dark gray towball-and-socket plate with a red 1x2 plate on top (b28, b29). Its socket takes the ball of the leg plate b24.

Step 17 attaches the finished leg to the body. The body socket isn't visible, so I assumed the free ball of b28 snaps into the light-gray socket plate b2. This conflicts with the eye edge I recorded earlier on the same socket.

Page 12 builds the same leg again (steps 1-3), and page 13 adds the same step 4 and attaches it in step 18, joined to socket b3. I wrote it out as separate parts rather than a repeat because it is mirrored.
Plate types are likely mislabelled. The parts list has only two 14417 plates, but I've now used four. The body plates b4 and b5 may actually be a different dark-gray plate type.
Pages 14-15 show step 19 as a rotate-the-model view with no callout, and page 16 is an advertisement page for the Mixels combination (41500/41501/41502 into Infernites Max).
The two trans-red flame pieces appear on the back of the model in the rotated views, but no earlier step showed them being added. I recorded them as added here.
I assumed each flame's bar is held in one of the arm clips (b8 and b11). This is a low-confidence guess because the views show the flames as one cluster at the back.
Pages 18-20 are advertising only: the Mixels series poster, the in-game code page and the product-feedback promo. They have no building steps, so nothing is added.

Arms: b7 and b10 were typed as 51739 wedge plates, but they are the red 1x4 hinge-with-clip plates (73983). I re-emitted them with the same ids and the corrected type. Their existing edges are unchanged. This fixes the 51739 excess and covers both 73983.
51739: the second wedge plate is the dark red front torso wedge that appears in step 16 (b39), so 51739 now matches the parts list at two (b16 and b39).
54200: step 12 shows a second dark red cheese slope on the other side of the head, added as b38. With b17, b26 and b32 that makes four.
93273: the dark red curved band across the mouth in step 16 is the 4x1 double curved brick (b40).

Not fixed: b4 and b5 are still typed 14417, which is two over the parts list. The legs already use the two 14417 plates (b24, b30). The two dark-gray body plates in step 2 are probably not that type, but I couldn't tell from the images what they really are, so I left them.

Not fixed: 3020 (x1), 3069b (x2), 3710 (x1) and 3794b (x3) are in the parts list but I couldn't find them in the booklet pages. They are probably hidden inside the dark red shell in steps 12 and 16 or are not shown in the views. I didn't invent placements for them.
Several stud ports and the step 16 and step 12 placements are approximate.

I can't remove earlier parts, so the excess counts for 14417 (x2) and 51739 (x2) can't be fixed by adding. Read the earlier entries as superseded: b4 and b5 (typed 14417) are not real pieces, and b7 and b10 (typed 51739) are the 73983 hinge plates re-emitted under the same ids in the previous turn. The real 14417 pieces are b24 and b30. The real 51739 pieces are b16 and b39.

Added the parts-list pieces I couldn't find in the booklet pages: 3020 (b41), 3069b x2 (b42, b43), 3710 (b44) and 3794b x3 (b45-b47). They are probably hidden under the dark red shell in steps 12 and 16 or are not distinguishable in the small images. Every piece in a Mixels set goes into the model.

The placements of those seven pieces are low-confidence guesses. The dark red 2x4 plate sits under the wedge b16 with the three jumper plates on it. The two red tiles smooth the tops of the foot plates b29 and b35. The red 1x4 plate sits on the inverted bracket b15.
I also kept the extra edges from the last turn.
